title: No W4 summary is inferred for a kinded result, out slot or release, and a tracked descriptor handed to a callee only a W4 summary covers is refused
why: Card W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING keeps inferred summaries heap-only: `propose_result` and `out_mode` decline a non-heap returned or delivered site, `result_matches` and `out_slots_match` require the declared kind, and a probed (heap) formal released by a descriptor or stream release is accused, so it validates no summary. A descriptor-returning body therefore certifies on its own but publishes nothing, and its callers see an uncontracted call: measured on the corpus, `mk_socket_create` (blocked also by `mk_utils_libc_error`), and the two librdkafka socket/open callbacks, which return the raw call result under a contract-free exit (`rd_kafka_open_cb_linux`, `rd_kafka_socket_cb_linux`: `nullable resource __qcore_returned_value used by a non-null contract`). The companion rule refuses a tracked descriptor at any position of a callee that no retained declaration covers, because a W4 `Borrowed` for an integer formal was derived with the formal untracked, so a helper that stores its formal into a member still earns it (the launder constraint 10 closed for pointers); it fired on no corpus leaf at the arbiter. Discharge condition: a kinded summary inference whose integer result is recognised only where every non-site exit returns the literal sentinel, and a formal-retention check for integer formals, each with Lean parity and a measured arbiter; or declared contracts for the wrappers.

title: Descriptor and handle callees refused by name: status-conditioned out list, command-dependent creator, array out slot, success-only transfer, unreadable prototypes, in-place lifecycle, pointer sentinel
why: Card W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING declared open, close, socket, fopen, fclose, fileno, opendir and closedir, and refused the rest of the descriptor family by name, measured at its AFTER baseline (leaves / functions / sole-blocked Unknown functions): `getaddrinfo` 4/4/0 and `freeaddrinfo` 6/4/0 (the out list is valid exactly when the call returns 0: needs a status witness bound to the slot; a nullable out slot would misstate the failure arm); `fcntl` 2/2/1 (a creator only for F_DUPFD/F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC; the units spell F_SETFL, F_GETFL, F_SETFD and F_SETLK, and one declaration carries one literal premise per parameter; `rd_kafka_open_cb_generic` is now blocked by it alone); `accept4` 1/1/0 (its `__SOCKADDR_ARG` transparent union is withdrawn by the declared-ABI census in all 93 declaring units; `accept` likewise, no leaf); `fts_open`/`fts_close` 1/1/0 each (`char * const *` and an inline comparator declarator: withdrawn in the one declaring unit, and the release alone decides nothing); `glob`/`globfree` 1/1/0 each (in-place lifecycle of a caller `glob_t` plus an error callback, W43-LIBC-IN-PLACE-LIFECYCLE's shape); `pipe` (an `int[2]` out slot; a descriptor has no out slot in this vocabulary), `fdopen` (transfer into the stream on success only), `mmap`/`munmap` (pointer sentinel MAP_FAILED): spelled in the units, no leaf of their own. `dup`, `dup2`, `creat`, `openat`, `mkstemp`, `popen`/`pclose`, `socketpair`, `epoll_create1`, `eventfd`, `timerfd_create`, `signalfd`, `inotify_init1` are called by no audited unit. Discharge condition: per shape, a vocabulary addition with gateway and Lean parity (status witness, per-command premise set, integer out slot, conditional transfer, pointer sentinel) or a reader repair, then per-callee declarations measured by an arbiter.

title: `return (T *)p;` is read as returning no place, so an acquisition returned through a cast is reported as a leak; dlopen/dlclose withheld on it
why: Measured by card W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING: the return route escapes `return p;` but answers a parenthesised cast of one place with no returned place, so the site stays live and `report_leaks` reports it at that exit, for the heap exactly as for a stream (`descriptor_custody.rs::a_cast_return_is_not_an_escape_for_any_kind`). Three of the 271 combined-tree leak leaves already sit at such an exit (`mk_string_copy_substr` 1, `rd_kafka_anyconf_dump` 2; scripts/cast_return_leaks.py). The card's first AFTER run declared dlopen/dlclose and moved `rd_dl_open0` Unknown -> provisional Unsafe with one leak at `return (rd_dl_hnd_t *)handle;` — a candidate refuted by reading, since the handle is returned. The pair and the `dynamic_library` kind were withdrawn before the published arbiter; they hold 5 leaves in 4 functions (`mk_plugin_load_dynamic`, `rd_dl_open0`, `mk_plugin_load`, `rd_dl_close`), dlopen and dlclose sole-blocking one function each. Discharge condition: the return route escapes the place under a pointer-to-pointer cast (the value is unchanged, C11 6.3.2.3p7) with Lean parity and an arbiter attributing every withdrawn leak, then the dlopen/dlclose declarations re-measured.

title: The kind-mismatched release and use-after-close candidates reach no function of the pinned corpus
why: Card W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING added `LegacyDiagnosticKind::KindMismatchedRelease` (published as invalid_release) and `UseAfterClose` (published as use_after_release), both read from settled states by `report_kind_violations`. They are unit-tested (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/descriptor_custody.rs: free(fopen), fclose(malloc), read after close, fflush after fclose) and modelled in QCore.KindedCustody, but the arbiter added zero leaves of either category: no audited function hands a handle of one kind to another kind's release or uses a released descriptor or stream at a declared position. The one candidate the declarations exposed is a leak (`ctr_random_get`'s `if (fd > 0)`). Discharge condition: a pinned or held-out real-code fixture reaching either arm, with the leaf attributed and never presented as an upstream defect.
